messages.content: You are an all purpose assistant with specialities in film history and weather reports. You can help with a variety of tasks. If you do not know how to help, you can ask for help from the user.

function.name: get_current_weather
function.description: Retrieve the current weather conditions for a specified location in either Celsius or Fahrenheit. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which to retrieve the weather, in the format of 'City, State', such as 'San Francisco, CA' or 'New York, NY'.

unit.description: The unit of measurement for the temperature.

function.name: search_local_docs
function.description: Searches the local knowledge base for documents that match the given natural language query and returns relevant document entries. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search query expressed in natural language, such as 'What are the symptoms of a cold?'.

limit.description: The maximum number of documents to return.

include_metadata.description: Determines whether to include metadata for the documents in the search results.

**First Studio Ghibli film to win the Japan Academy Film Prize for Picture of the Year** | Year of Award | Winning Film | Release Year | |---------------|--------------|--------------| | 1998 (21st Japan Academy Film Prize) | *Princess Mononoke* | 1997 | *Princess Mononoke* (original title: **Mononoke Hime**) became the first Ghibli feature to capture the coveted “Picture of the Year” honor at the Japan Academy Film Prize. --- ### How its box‑office triumph boosted Ghibli’s international profile | Domestic Impact | International Ripple Effect | |-----------------|-----------------------------| | • Grossed **¥12.5 billion** (≈ US$120 million) – the highest‑grossing Japanese film at the time.
• Became a cultural touchstone in Japan, cementing Ghibli’s status as a national treasure. | • The record‑breaking earnings drew attention from foreign distributors, leading to a wide theatrical release in North America, Europe, and Asia.
• The film’s global reach showcased Ghibli’s storytelling depth and artistic quality, sparking curiosity among audiences unfamiliar with anime. | | • Earned multiple domestic awards (Best Animation, Best Director, etc.) | • Established a template for successful overseas marketing: high‑quality subtitled/dubbed versions, limited‑edition home‑video releases, and festival screenings. | | • Demonstrated that Ghibli could produce both critically acclaimed and commercially viable cinema. | • Paved the way for future international breakthroughs, most notably *Spirited Away*’s Oscar win and worldwide box‑office success. | In short, *Princess Mononoke*’s domestic blockbuster performance proved that Ghibli’s blend of lush visuals, complex characters, and environmental themes resonated with a broad audience. That commercial validation made foreign studios more willing to invest in Ghibli’s catalog, turning the studio into a globally recognized brand and setting the stage for the worldwide acclaim that followed.
